text: Longitudinal clinical cohorts following individuals, who are born to parents with severe mental illness, from childhood into adulthood, provide invaluable insight into development of psychopathology, illness course over time and risk and resilience factors. Further, initiatives to prevent mental illness and support families at risk can be inspired and informed. The Danish High Risk and Resilience Study - the VIA cohort was founded during 2013-2015, where 522 7-year-old individuals born to parents with either schizophrenia bipolar disorder or controls, were recruited together with their parents and thoroughly examined. This study protocol presents the VIA 19 study, which is the fourth wave of the study investigating mental health and neurodevelopment in the 19-year-old participants, now in early adulthood.
source_label: Study protocol for the Danish High Risk and Resilience Study VIA 19 – from age 15 to age 19: transition from adolescence to early adulthood
